issue_context.title: Tado Smart AC incorrectly switches to 'Cool' mode if temperature changed.
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->
Tado Smart AC running in Heat mode (set externally via Tado App or SmartSchedule) switches to Cool if you change the temperature in Home Assistant (instead of remaining in 'Heat' mode).

Home Assistant then reports the mode as now being 'Heat/Cool', but Tado actually switches to Cool when temperature is changed via Home Assistant.

Not a problem in summer when it's hot and the AC is running Cool anyway, but a bit iffy in Winter when you try to turn the heating up and end up making it colder..

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 
0.106.0
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 
unknown
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): 
Docker/Ubuntu Server
- Integration causing this issue:
Issue with Tado (Climate)
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tado 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

# Tado Smart Thermostat
tado:
  username: !secret tado_username
  password: !secret tado_password

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

No errors - it thinks it's working!

## Additional information
I suspect that when changing the temperate the hvac mode may not be being sent, or is defaulted to Cool (as it's an AC unit)
 
Found the below in the OpenHab documentation (which was linked to in a tado forum as having reasonably good info about the API)
https://community.tado.com/en-gb/discussion/8/tado-api
https://www.openhab.org/addons/bindings/tado/
(Having said that, I don't know if the fallback referenced below is an API behaviour, or an Openhab behaviour) 

Relevant Section:
#Default Handling
To set an override, the tado° cloud API requires a full setting (hvacMode, targetTemperature, fanspeed, swing) and a termination condition (operationMode, timerDuration). If only some of the properties are set, the binding fills the missing pieces automatically. It tries to keep the current state wherever possible.

If parts of the setting are missing, then the currently active zone setting is used to fill the gap. Only if the setting is not compatible with the requested change, then hard-coded defaults are applied.

hvacMode is set to HEAT for heating and hot water, and set to COOL for AC
targetTemperature for heating is 22°C / 72°F, AC is set to 20°C / 68°F and hot water to 50°C / 122°F
fanspeed is set to first supported value, for example AUTO
swing is set to OFF, if supported
If the termination condition is missing, the binding first checks if an override is active. If that is the case, the existing termination condition is used. An existing timer, for example, just keeps running. In case the zone is currently in smart-schedule mode and thus doesn't have a termination condition, then the default termination condition is used, as configured in the tado° app (settings -> select zone -> manual control on tado° device).

Here are the attributes/states for the Tado AC unit entity :-

hvac_modes:
  - heat_cool
  - auto
  - 'off'
min_temp: 15
max_temp: 30
target_temp_step: 1
preset_modes:
  - away
  - home
current_temperature: 21
temperature: 15
current_humidity: 51.9
hvac_action: idle
preset_mode: home
friendly_name: Air Conditioning
supported_features: 17

I think 'Heat' and 'Cool' should be two different modes (which is how they present in the Tado app), rather than a combined mode... (The tado app has a toggle, which flips between heat and cool every time you tap it)

@bdraco 
Definite improvement!

Behaviour is good, with a couple of inconsistencies:

If you change the mode on the thermostat card to heat or cold first and then change the temperature, the correct mode and temperate register in the tado app and everything behaves as expected.

If you change temperature in HA in auto then nothing happens. No mode or temperature change occurs within the tado app. The set temperature numeric display on the thermostat card and the slider seemingly remains where you set it until the page is refreshed/reloaded (at which point it reverts to the auto/smartschedule settings). 

If in auto and you set the temperate first, _then_ change the mode, the set temperature numeric reverts to the current tado settings although the slider remains at it's set position instead of updating. The mode changes in tado correctly, but at the same last temperature from the smart schedule instead of the temperate set before the mode change.
Changing the temperature in HA then works as expected.

If HA has the thermo set to off and you change the temperate nothing happens, but if then then change the mode to heat or cool the mode correctly changes and uses the temperature set via the slider (as opposed to reverting to last active temp).

Finally, if in auto and the tado is actively running heating mode, the thermostat card incorrectly shows as "cooling" instead of "heating".
The card correctly displays as off when in auto and the tado is idle and correctly shows as cooling when in auto and actively cooling but can't be sure if the latter is just because of defaults).

@gvdhoven 

Just did a very quick test, and yes, you can be affected, but you can work around it by chaining together the service calls.

Calling climate.set_temperature forces mine into cool mode even if I specify _hvac_mode: heat_ in the service call.

But if I then call climate.set_hvac_mode explicitly I can specify heat or cool and it sticks.

So if using service calls in an automation/script for your schedule, set the temperature as one action, then set the hvac mode as the next action to correctly set the mode you want.

If you're using the front end card control, click the heat or cool icon first, and then set the temperature (although if you're already showing as in the mode you want, you're ok).

Behaviour might be slightly different for you, because a lot of it depends on the capabilities of the unit you've got it connected to and I think that affects the capabilities declared by the integration.

Hope this helps, and it would be great if you can confirm the behaviour you're seeing.
